Decode: `python3 -c 'import json,gzip,base64,sys; e=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); open(e[\"filename\"],\"wb\").write(gzip.decompress(base64.b64decode(e[\"payload\"])))' envelope.json` after saving the JSON block below to envelope.json.\n\n```json\n{\"filename\": \"bt-table-a067c53-73dd98b8.txt\", \"bytes\": 114756, \"sha256\": \"6c4ed7acde47c3a40a8c803b01d4267419da25c7fbc7bad5cf77daa6efe44776\", \"encoding\": \"gzip+base64\", \"source\": \"sawtracker a067c53 (src/ tree), compiler ~/Projects/sawlang 73dd98b8 (no local modifications), bin/sawc --emit-<report> src/main.saw, 2026-09-23 EDT, macOS/arm64\", \"payload\": \"\"}\n```\n","created":"1790174203","id":"c7"}],"created":"1790117213","description":"# A struct literal with a memory destination is built IN PLACE; a coroutine frame is initialised by stores and a zero-fill, never as an `insertvalue` chain\n\nRULED by the user Sep 22 2026 (SL-341 c4 option B). Fixes SL-341 (the AArch64 machine-scheduler assertion) and SL-336 (the 65535-flattened-values overflow) at the one emission both come from. Implementer: any — the user intends codex; the lead validates on submission per the patch flow. Isolated from design 275 U3 (`sl318u3`): U3 touches the typechecker, `coro_transform.py`'s splits and `codegen/loops.py`; this brief touches `codegen/structs.py`'s literal lowering, the `let`/assignment funnel it lands in, and `_build_frame_init`'s shape. Build in an own worktree from main; rebase after SL-318.p7 lands (hunk by hunk on `coro_transform.py` if anything overlaps).\n\n## 0. The finding (SL-341 sweep, Sep 22, SL-341 c3)\n\nFour sawtracker resumes (`main`, `run_store`, `response`, `dispatch`) each hold one ~4000-instruction straight-line block: 2959-4078 `insertvalue` plus ~800 `Slot$…_empty()` calls over 39 distinct aggregate types — the WHOLE embedded frame tree materialised as ONE SSA aggregate value and then stored into `__f`. LLVM 22.1.0's AArch64 pre-RA scheduler asserts on that block (`RegisterPressure.cpp:1350`), and the same emission at 65535+ flattened values overflows `visitInsertValue` (SL-336). Nothing in the sawlang corpus is within 4× of the shape, but it grows with the transitive embedded frame tree of any suspending call graph, so every program of sawtracker's depth reaches it.\n\nThe mechanism, in source: `coro_transform._build_frame_init` (~:9490) returns a `StructInit` for the frame whose fields are params, `_zeroed_value(...)` for every local, and — RECURSIVELY — a `StructInit` for every embedded callee's dead sub-frame; `codegen/structs.py::_generate_struct_init` (~:26) evaluates each field and builds the aggregate with `insert_value` (the loop at `codegen/methods.py:359` is the same pattern for another literal). A nested literal nests the chain; the frame's `let __f = <init>` then stores the finished value.\n\n## 1. The rules\n\n**R1 — a struct literal whose value LANDS IN MEMORY is built in place.** When the destination is known — a `let`/`var` initializer (the frame's `__f` included), an assignment RHS, a field initializer of an enclosing in-place literal, an array/collection-literal element being stored, a `static` initializer that is not const-folded — `_generate_struct_init` receives the destination POINTER and emits one store per field through a GEP (recursing into nested literals with the field's GEP as THEIR destination), and returns nothing to insert. The SSA path (`insert_value`) remains ONLY where the value is consumed as an SSA value with no destination: a by-value call argument, a `return` of a literal, an operand. ONE funnel decides: `_materialize_struct_init(expr, dest_ptr)` — docstring names every entry (obligation 1); `dest_ptr=None` is the SSA path.\n\n**R2 — an all-zero subtree is one zero-fill.** `_build_frame_init` marks (a declared annotation field, design 126) which of its field initializers are entirely dead state — `_zeroed_value` locals, dead sub-frames, `__state`/`__wake`/`__io_*` zeros, `__cancel` false — and the in-place lowering emits ONE `llvm.memset(0)` over the frame (or the largest zero run) followed by stores of only the NON-ZERO fields (params, `__recv`, `__cellp`, `__io_fd = -1`, a `Some`-wrapped opt-encoded param). PRECONDITION to verify first: `Slot<T>.empty()`'s bit pattern is all-zero (the `std.compiler.frame` docstring says empty is \"the not-yet-live state\"; confirm with `--emit-ir` on a one-slot frame — if a tag byte is non-zero, the zero-fill covers everything else and the tag is a store). Nested dead sub-frames are then zero bytes, not calls.\n\n**R3 — nothing observable changes.** Field values, evaluation ORDER of field initializers (left to right as written — a side-effecting initializer runs where it ran), destruction (the frame's `__release`, drop flags), the frame LAYOUT (`--emit-frame-layout`, the bt-table, `--emit-frame-ledger` are all layout/discovery instruments — byte-identical before and after), and the copy/transfer decisions at a field (`_generate_copy_for_dest`, `_coerce_int_to_field`) all hold; only the instruction sequence that writes the bytes changes.\n\n## 2. Units (one branch, commit order)\n\n1. **Pins first:** an `examples/` program with a struct literal at every R1 destination position (and the SSA positions as controls) printing field values + a deinit-order trace; SL-336's repro (a frame flattening past 65535 values — build it from the issue) as a compile-and-run example; a `for`-of-frames stress that measures nothing but must run. The sawtracker acceptance is external (below).\n2. **The funnel** (`_materialize_struct_init`, its entries routed, SSA path untouched) — gate; design-220 IR compare against main classifying every changed function (expected: every struct-literal site in the corpus changes instruction sequence, none changes behaviour; `reemit` + `irdet --all` prove determinism).\n3. **The zero-fill** (R2) — gate; census: the biggest frame-init block per function over the corpus artifacts (the sweep's metric, `.build/test_runner_last/*.ll`) and over sawtracker's post-build `.ll`, before/after.\n4. **Docs:** LANGUAGE_SPEC's coroutine-frame section gets one sentence (a frame is zero-filled then written; nothing user-visible); `designs/todo.md` entry closed in place; SL-341 + SL-336 close at landing with the sawtracker result.\n\n## 3. Obligations\n\n- **Obligation 1:** R1 is position-quantified → the one funnel with named entries + the per-position pin.\n- **Obligation 2 (consumer sweep — who reads a struct literal's SSA value):** every `_generate_struct_init` caller and every consumer of `StructInit` in codegen (`_gen_transfer_value`, the argument path, `return`, the `??`/branch merges in `conditionals.py:435-468` that `insert_value` a wrapped literal), the spawn helpers that build a frame and hand it to the group cell, `_read_frame_result`, `__release`, the enum-payload construction at `calls.py:3512-3572` (DF-300a's byte-shred — same family, say whether it joins R1 or stays), `--emit-frame-layout`/bt-table (layout readers, unaffected), the `reemit`/`irdet`/`corodiff` lanes.\n- **Obligation 4:** the class is \"an aggregate built as an SSA value and then stored\"; the enum-payload and optional-wrap constructions are its siblings — probe their worst corpus sizes and say whether they are within reach of either LLVM limit; R1 covers them if they route through the funnel.\n\n## 4. Acceptance + gates\n\nACCEPTANCE (external, run by the implementer read-only and by the lead): `sawc src/main.saw` in `/Users/shawn/Projects/sawtracker` at the DEFAULT level → EXIT 0 (today: the assertion), and the binary passes sawtracker's integration suite (today: only via `SAWLINK=clang`); the sweep's `slice_743_nodbg.ll` stays as the LLVM-side pin but is no longer producible. Compile-time delta on sawtracker recorded (the 76,000-line resume shrinks). Per-commit: full suite + freestanding both arches; terminal: full battery (32 stages) — `reemit`, `irdet --all`, `corodiff`, `freestanding` are the lanes this brief can break. No XFAIL; SL-336's pin must PASS (no marker), or the brief is not done.\n\n## 5. Out of scope\n\nThe llvmlite version (C in SL-341 c4); design 263's field-read narrowing beyond what R1 needs; SL-347's sweep (parallel, `.saw`-only, no overlap).\n","id":"SL-350","labels":["design","codegen","coroutine"],"order":0,"parent":"","priority":"high","project":"SL","queue_order":0,"revision":10,"sequence":1248,"stage":"queued","status":"open","title":"Design (RULED Sep 22): a struct literal with a memory destination is built IN PLACE; a coroutine frame is zero-filled then written, never an insertvalue chain — fixes SL-341 + SL-336 at their one emission","updated":"1790174203"},"before":{"acceptance":[],"assignee":"agent:codex","author":"agent:claude-sawlang","closed":"","comments":[{"author":"agent:codex","body":"Implementation and independent validation in progress, not submitted.
